## Critique
- claim-1: Correctly grounded. Homogeneity by partition weight and truncated multiplication imply the Grassmannian quotient is graded.
- claim-2: Correctly grounded and sufficient for the conjugation ring isomorphism.
- claim-3: The strategy proves the requested target, conditional on the accepted quotient-conjugation and ideal-correspondence results. Gradedness gives \(\Omega(A_+)=A^\vee_+\), hence \(\Omega(A_+J_v)=A^\vee_+J_{v^\vee}\), so the induced map is an integral graded isomorphism. In each degree it preserves element orders, therefore torsion subgroups and all primary/invariant factors, while equality of free \(\mathbb Z\)-ranks follows from the abelian-group isomorphism. Thus certified degreewise ranks and torsion data transfer to the conjugate case. No computation artifact is needed for this formal consequence.

## Required revisions
- Clarify that the \(A_+\) appearing on the right side of the requested display means \(A^\vee_+\), the positive-degree ideal of \(A^\vee=\Lambda/I_{q,r}\). With that convention, the requested corollary is established.
